text:
maya: Heads-up — after last night's proxy tweak, a bunch of EU WS clients started doing tight reconnect loops. Dashboard shows small spike in sessions but large token/billing churn.
ashwin: Any chance it's just a client library bug? which route/edge?
maya: EU edge (eu-west-1), route /v1/stream/ws. Proxy change was enabling quiet-close (send 204 then FIN) to avoid long-lived sockets. Logs show client sees 204 -> immediately reconnects, sometimes 2x per second.
joel: 204 is meant for pollers. For WS/SSE we should prefer a graceful close handshake so clients can resume vs restart. Did we strip resume tokens on that path?
maya: looks like resume token header was being dropped by the proxy when responding 204. server side didn't see resume so it treated reconnect as fresh session.
kelsey: That explains billing churn. Console counts increments on new session creation, not resumes. UX wise we show sessions started, so SREs will freak out.
ryan: Quick patch idea: have the proxy attach a short wait-window header (x-ws-wait-ms: 3000) on quiet-close so clients with resume logic backoff for TTL. Clients could honor wait and try resume.
nashwin: But forcing clients to change is risky. We should handle idempotency server-side — if we can detect recently closed session with same client-id/resume-token, treat as resume for 10s. cheaper.
joel: Detecting requires us to keep tombstones for session ids for window T. Memory + index cost but feasible in gateway. Need telemetry to estimate hit-rate first.
kelsey: Also need console telemetry: resume_rate, duplicate_session_rate, billing_delta per-route. Product wants an annotation on the route page.
infra-bot: Canary deploy 01 completed at 1876543225 on proxy-v2 (quiet-close enabled).
maya: repro snippet from logs (simplified):
```
PROXY eu-west-1 - client 10.4.2.18 - GET /v1/stream/ws -> 204 quiet-close
client lib - sees 204 -> OPEN ws connection -> sends Authorization, no resume header -> server creates session id s_abc123
```
ryan: Two approaches: 1) proxy preserves resume header on quiet-close + adds wait header, 2) gateway keeps short-lived tombstones and treats immediate reconnects as resumes.
ashwin: Option 1 is lower risk and faster to roll back. Option 2 is more correct but touches hot path.
joel: Also consider console distinction: show "resumes" vs "new sessions" in the timeline so ops can tell if it's churn or growth. That requires event tagging in telemetry pipeline.
kelsey: Agree. For immediate mitigation -> toggle quiet-close off for WS routes in the canary group and push an alert rule to watch duplicate session rate > 5% over baseline.
maya: I'll flip the flag on canary and add a short-lived dashboard panel for duplicate_session_rate.
ryan: I'll prototype tombstones in gateway (+metrics). If it looks cheap we can promote.
nashwin: I'll open a tiny client-facing doc recommending honoring x-ws-wait-ms and planning a minor client lib release.
deploy-bot: Rollout action created: rollback-quiet-close-canary #1427 by maya.
maya: thanks — will update once canary stabilizes. :thumbsup:
